title: Project Brief — T4 (retrospective, 2026-11-22)
body:
# Project brief — T4 Kanban coach (retrospective, 2026-11-22)

## Outcome

The conveyor has a coach loop for an interruption. A failed run opens exactly one coach card with one triage and one remedy from the seeded closed catalogue; a repeat signature escalates instead of opening a second card; a failed coach run opens no coach card and a nested coach run is refused; and a systemic class starts `kata.open`. The first-interruption shape, escalation and the depth cap are live and proved by named tests; four findings remain open, and v1-p6-4 shows the 'exactly one' does not hold for a fourth distinct signature.

## Boundary

T4 owns the interruption row, the coach card, its triage and remedy, the per-signature escalation rule and the depth cap. It does not own the board and pull path that calls `err.card`, the kata's own lifecycle and measurement (T5), the PM job (T3), operations incidents and postmortems (T7), or the tool platform (T13). T4 starts a kata process; it does not build the kata.

## Reuse sources

`migrations/0057_coach.sql` — `coach_interruption` and `coach_remedy`. `crates/actions/src/coach.rs` — `coach.interrupt`, `open_interruption_tx`, `record_triage_tx`, `insert_remedy_tx`, `mark_escalated_tx`, `is_coach_card_tx` and `set_kata_candidate_tx`. The board card store and `cards.create`. The seeded process catalogue and its idempotent seed. The approval gates `coach.ask` and `coach.escalation`. The real-Postgres action test harness.

## Inception units

No T4-specific inception analysis or architecture design is present in the snapshot; this rework authored none. The inception claim is the SPEC_V2 sections 6.2 and 6.4 text, the T4 row of section 12 and the issue #75 body. The implementation record is the coach action module, the 0057 migration and the two suites.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: T3 and P0 (`project.meta.depends_on = [T3, P0]`); the coach writes cards and gates on the board and approval spine T3 and T1 install.
- blocks: T7 (operations severity and the gate pre-check) and T12 (the one organisation loop), per the section 12 dependency line.
- related: T5 (the kata the systemic class opens) and T10 (the cadence retro card the coach owns).

## Acceptance

The SPEC_V2 section 12 T4 gate: an injected failure yields exactly one coach card and one remedy; a repeat signature escalates; no coach card about a coach card; a systemic class opens a kata. Clauses 2 and 3 are green by `coach.rs`; clause 1 is green for a first interruption and red for a fourth distinct signature (v1-p6-4); clause 4 is green as a process start and incomplete as a kata record (v1-p6-2). The rework's acceptance instrument is `acceptance/programme/T4.toml`.

## Capabilities

One card, one triage and one remedy; per-signature escalation; the depth cap; the closed triage and remedy catalogue; the systemic-class `kata.open` start; the stored interruption, triage and remedy rows.

## Plan

Held to `docs/SPEC_V2.md` section 12 (T4) and sections 6.2 and 6.4. The project row's plan pointer is `docs/SPEC_V2.md#12` with `plan_status: draft`; no separate plan document exists. The project row is closed in the 2026-11-22 snapshot (version 10); the rework records the lifecycle retrospectively.

## Risks

- The per-card cap drops a fourth distinct signature (v1-p6-4): a real interruption can get no card and no owner.
- Only failed runs produce interruptions (v1-p6-5): WIP breaches, stale leases, gate timeouts and board events have no coach path.
- The systemic class opens only a process run (v1-p6-2): no instrument, threshold, measurement or adoption gate.
- `cards.create` can mint an orphan coach card (v1-p6-6).
- Tranche 4 is `planned` with no authorisation review, `authorised_at` or baseline; T4 closed out of sequence.
